name: @vssaros/dsh-web-content-import
description: VsSaros web-content-import module for DeepSeek Harness: a single `content_import` tool that resolves a URL (platform article / video), fetches its content (HTTP + reader for static pages, yt-dlp + whisper ASR for videos, caller-fed HTML for login-walled pages), and optionally writes it into the knowledge base (库/raw/<slug>.md). 落盘契约与 IDE 侧 kbUrlScraper / web-content-import 技能逐字对齐；方案见 doc/dsh-content-import-plan.md。0.1.4 adds a BATCH entry (urls[]): a URL list from a crawler / platform search / export can be imported in one call instead of N - processed SERIALLY (these sites rate-limit, and serial makes per-item progress reportable), each item isolated by its own try/catch so one failure never aborts the batch, url and urls are merged and de-duplicated, and the queue is capped at 20 (beyond that the tool call hits its timeout - batch it up). Returns { count, ok, results[] } with per-item url / ok / status / title / saved / error; the single-URL path is untouched (the batch wrapper is layered ON TOP of the existing lossless-json wrapper, so the normal path is byte-identical). Implemented because discovery (finding URLs) and understanding (reading one article well) are separate concerns - this plugin only does the latter, and batching is what lets it consume a crawler's output. 0.1.5 adds `urlFile`: read the URL list straight from a file instead of pasting links into the tool call. Four formats are supported and auto-detected - .txt (one URL per line), .jsonl (MediaCrawler's JSONL writer), .json (array, or wrapped as {contents:[...]}), and .csv (quoted fields). Extraction prefers a known field-name list (note_url / aweme_url / content_url / url / share_url / link / href ...), then falls back to scanning the object tree for any http(s) string, so unknown crawler schemas still work; image/static-asset URLs are filtered out; order is preserved and duplicates removed (order carries search relevance). Pure function in lib/core/urlList.js (no IO) so it is unit-testable and reusable from the IDE side. Verified with 7 format cases + empty input. Note the plugin's files whitelist had to gain lib/core/urlList.js - omitting it is exactly the kind of thing that only fails after packaging. 0.1.6 fixes de-duplication identity after verifying MediaCrawler's real field names: all seven platforms are covered by URL_FIELDS (xhs/weibo/tieba use note_url, douyin uses aweme_url, bilibili/kuaishou use video_url, zhihu uses content_url) - but xhs note_url carries a short-lived `xsec_token` query, so the same note arriving from two searches has two different URLs and de-duplicating on the full URL would import it twice. Dedupe key is now origin + pathname (query and hash ignored), and when two variants of the same note are seen the one carrying xsec_token wins (xhs frequently fails to resolve without it). Added a regression case for exactly this. 0.1.7 documents the freshness constraint where it will actually be read: the urlFile parameter description now warns that xhs links carry a short-lived xsec_token, so import must happen right after crawling - hours later the token is dead and fetching gets rejected; when that happens re-crawl for fresh tokens instead of retrying the stale link. Placed on the parameter (not the top-level description) because it is read exactly at the moment the model is about to batch-import a crawler's output.
